items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: And my older son, Jimmy, he’d play on the table

ctx.x: In six months she was working. In two years she was working with Phyllis Hyman. Yeah she’s done really well. They showed musical talent — my middle daughter, when she was four, could sing any note I could hit on the piano. I’d try to play the most unlikely, the oddest intervals, F to B, octave low to B flat or to A or whatever. And I’d say, “Sing it honey” and she was four years old. The keyboard came up to here on her and she’d sing it clear as a bell. Any interval I could think. I’d just hit intervals at…
wasn’t until she started playing that she just astounded me. To me she really is a great player, one of my favorite bass players. And I don’t say that because she’s my daughter.
